subject: history_social
passage: Mangoes from Pakistan have long been sent abroad by air, because ripe fruit spoils quickly. Refrigerated shipping containers, however, can keep mangoes fresh for the weeks needed to cross the sea, and they cost far less per tonne than air freight. Trade economist Bilal Qureshi, who examined records kept by an association of mango exporters in Multan, argues that the growth in the association's exports after 2010 came almost entirely from sea freight, while the quantity of mangoes its members sent by air hardly changed.

data.title: Mangoes Shipped Abroad by Members of a Multan Exporters' Association

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support Qureshi's argument?

choices.A: Total shipments rose from about 52,000 tonnes in 2010 to about 89,000 tonnes in 2018.
choices.B: In every year shown, members shipped more mangoes by sea than they did by air.
choices.C: From 2010 to 2018, air shipments and sea shipments increased by similar amounts.
choices.D: Sea shipments more than doubled from 2010 to 2018, while air shipments stayed between 21,000 and 24,000 tonnes.

explanation.why: Qureshi's argument is about the source of the growth: sea freight grew while air freight stayed nearly flat. Support must describe how each line changed. Sea shipments rose from 30 to 66 thousand tonnes, more than double, while air shipments stayed between 21 and 24 thousand tonnes.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is true, but it shows only that exports grew, which Qureshi takes for granted; it does not show which kind of shipping produced the growth.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true, but sea freight could exceed air freight every year without being the source of the growth.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Sea shipments rose by 36,000 tonnes, while air shipments rose by only 1,000, so this misreads the graph.
explanation.D: Correct. It shows strong growth in sea shipments alongside nearly flat air shipments, which is exactly the pattern Qureshi describes.
